contextBody: Ontario privacy commissioner says video surveillance can create privacy risks and provides guidance on appropriateness, retention, notice and disclosure for public institutions; applicability to private businesses varies by governing law.
sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

cctv.heading: CCTV and privacy
cctv.body: Before deployment, define purpose, field of view, notice, access to recordings and retention. The cited guidance is jurisdiction- and entity-specific; ask which privacy rules govern this site.
cctv.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

access.heading: Access control and egress
access.body: Confirm exit function, lock hardware and release behaviour with the building/fire authority. Provincial source describes building/fire plan review; it does not determine approval for a particular access-control change.
access.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

intrusion.heading: Intrusion detection planning
intrusion.body: Ask about monitored zones, authorized contacts, alarm verification and false-alarm procedures. The provincial source does not establish a province-wide intrusion alarm process.
intrusion.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

remote.heading: Remote escalation
remote.body: Ask who receives alerts, escalation order, response window and contact-update responsibility. These are project questions, not provincial facts established by the cited source.
remote.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

smart.heading: Smart-building energy
smart.body: Ontario says its energy and water reporting/benchmarking initiative helps building owners track performance and identify efficiency opportunities. Ask whether the property falls within the reporting program and what baseline data exists.
smart.sourceTitle: Report energy and water use in large buildings

cyber.heading: Cybersecurity
cyber.body: Ask about network segmentation, credentials, updates, vendor access and incident handling for connected systems. No province-wide technical standard is asserted here.
cyber.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

consulting.heading: Consulting and risk planning
consulting.body: Begin with a site-specific inventory, threat and privacy assessment, life-safety interfaces and documented assumptions. These are planning prompts, not provincial legal requirements.
consulting.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance

guards.heading: Guard operations
guards.body: Ask what duties, site instructions, training and escalation arrangements are needed. No licensing claim or province-specific guard requirement is made.
guards.sourceTitle: Guidelines for the Use of Video Surveillance
